clue.text: Port can make you sleep, man!

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
Les is a man's first name, short for Leslie

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims to a friend that a glass of port will send them off to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink, given 'sleep'; it is a harbour city in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Naples is a major seaport city on the bay of the same name in southern Italy.

clue.text: Affair in the morning taking sixty minutes first off

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks a time in the morning

indicators.note: first off says the opening letter of the word for sixty minutes is dropped

parts.note: sixty minutes make one hour

explanation.surface: A dalliance squeezed into an early hour before work, taking only one hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' drops the H from HOUR, leaving OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a French loan word for a love affair, especially a secret one.

clue.text: Materials in layers in a salt mine possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of a salt mine could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Geology talk: the strata exposed in a salt mine could be layered rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Laminates are sheet products built by bonding thin layers together.

clue.text: Element in society taking blame

parts.note: odium is general blame or disgrace attached to someone

explanation.surface: A section of society is being held responsible for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium is a soft metallic chemical element, symbol Na.

clue.text: End suffering setback after knave makes huge gains

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the word for knave

parts.note: the knave is the jack in a pack of cards

indicators.note: a setback turns things back, so the word for end is read backwards

parts.note: to end something is to stop it

explanation.surface: A villain's run of bad luck finishes and he suddenly makes a killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackpots are the largest prizes in games of chance, so big wins or windfalls.

clue.text: Banged intruders up in horrible jail in accordance with the law

indicators.note: in puts one jumbled set of letters inside the other
horrible suggests jail is a mess, so its letters are rearranged too
banged as in knocked about, so the letters of intruders up are jumbled

explanation.surface: Burglars have been locked up in a grim prison, as the law requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banged up' is British slang for jailed, so the surface reads as a prison sentence; cryptically 'Banged' and 'horrible' are both anagram signals, and 'in' nests one jumble inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Jurisprudential relates to jurisprudence, the theory and philosophy of law.

clue.text: Brilliant diet's start — tucking into lettuce and apples

indicators.note: tucking into says the pieces are placed inside the word for lettuce

parts.note: cos is a long-leaved variety of lettuce (romaine)
a star is someone brilliant at something

indicators.note: start says only the first letter of diet is used

explanation.surface: A star dieter's opening move is to tuck into a salad and fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucking into' looks like eating, but it is the container signal; 'apples' looks like part of the salad, yet it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Costards are a large old English variety of cooking apple.

clue.text: Name of female priest meeting lord

parts.note: an earl is a British nobleman, a lord

explanation.surface: A woman cleric is introduced to an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearl is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Something stuck on story still to be read out

indicators.note: read out says the words are spoken, so we want their sound

parts.note: a story is a tale, and still in the noun sense is peace or quiet

explanation.surface: A story has a piece stuck onto it that nobody has read aloud yet.
explanation.walkthrough: TALE PEACE sounds like the answer; 'still' as a noun means calm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailpiece is an addition at the end of something, such as a decoration closing a chapter.

clue.text: Naval officers keeping gold in small sideboards

indicators.note: in places the word for gold inside the word for small sideboards

parts.note: commodes are low chests of drawers or small cabinets
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Senior sailors are hoarding bullion in their cabinets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' just joins the definition to the wordplay; OR is the heraldic term for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Commodores rank above captains in a navy, commanding squadrons of ships.

clue.text: Not in favour of an alcoholic drink

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, here giving a single letter
gin is a juniper-flavoured spirit

explanation.surface: Someone declares themselves opposed to having a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect form of against, meaning opposed.

clue.text: It is one of them

parts.note: the clue's own words it and them are each a part of speech standing in for a noun

explanation.definitionFit: Words such as it, they and them replace nouns, which is the grammatical class asked for.

clue.text: Like run on an incline

parts.note: as means like, in a comparison
to lope is to run with a long easy stride

explanation.surface: A ski run that tilts down a hillside.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslope is a literary adverb or adjective meaning tilted or sloping.

clue.text: Bottle that's deposited on a cold winter's night

definitions.text: that's deposited on a cold winter's night

explanation.surface: Courage needed on a freezing night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage or nerve; also coarse sand is spread on icy roads by council gritters in winter.

clue.text: Minor star is upset as the result of depression

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of minor star are tumbled

explanation.surface: A lesser celebrity is distraught because they are feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' is not low mood but a weather system of low pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-pressure weather system often brings heavy rain and wind.

clue.text: Trad idea made to look silly and thrown out

indicators.note: making something look silly means distorting it, so the letters of trad idea are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned notion is mocked and discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat or light that is emitted spreads outwards from a source.

clue.text: Recognise cop

explanation.definitionFit: To understand or grasp something is one sense; to arrest, as a policeman nabs a suspect, is the other.

clue.text: When stirred up, Eva and faith get very angry

indicators.note: stirred up means mixed around, so the letters of Eva and faith are shuffled together

explanation.surface: Eva and her faith are agitated until someone loses their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be furious or have a sudden outburst of temper.

clue.text: Trees I'd planted, bringing in volunteers to give emergency help

indicators.note: bringing in places the letters for volunteers inside the others

parts.note: firs are evergreen conifers
I'd without its apostrophe
the TA, the Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A tree-planting volunteer group also offers medical help in emergencies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'planted' is surface only; TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's former name for its army reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: First aid is the immediate treatment given to an injured person before a doctor arrives.

clue.text: Stay around to get a sly look

indicators.note: around signals turning the word for stay the other way round

parts.note: to keep is to stay or remain

explanation.surface: Someone loiters nearby to sneak a glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A peek is a quick furtive glance.

clue.text: Frustrated father grabbing the girl maybe

indicators.note: grabbing says the word for father holds the pronoun inside

parts.note: dad is father
she is the pronoun for a girl, hence maybe

explanation.surface: An exasperated dad snatches hold of his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashed hopes are ruined or thwarted ones, as with frustrated plans.

clue.text: Not entirely serious, a blemish — if something's this?

definitions.text: Not entirely serious, a blemish — if something's this?

indicators.note: not entirely says only part of the words serious, a blemish is used

explanation.surface: A minor flaw on an item may still leave it fit for purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across 'serioUS A BLEmish'; the whole clue then explains it: a flaw that is not serious leaves a thing still serviceable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with only a minor defect is still fit to be used.

clue.text: What percussionist plays? No good — jeer goes round

indicators.note: goes round says the jeer encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: boo is a jeer of disapproval

explanation.surface: A drummer is so bad the audience jeers.
explanation.definitionFit: A bongo is a small hand drum played in pairs.

clue.text: Area to have comfy home in? On the contrary, maybe!

definitions.text: Area to have comfy home in? On the contrary, maybe!

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another
on the contrary swaps the roles, so the comfy home holds the area rather than the reverse

parts.note: a nest is a snug home

explanation.surface: Someone wonders which region would be the place to settle cosily.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, AREA would hold NEST; 'On the contrary' flips it so NEST holds AREA. 'maybe' marks the answer as one example of an area.
explanation.definitionFit: The Near East is a region of countries around the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: What brings enchantment for short time

explanation.surface: Magic that lasts only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: An incantation casts enchantment; also a period, as in a cold snap or a brief stint.

clue.text: Heartless fool to make very rude gesture

indicators.note: heartless means the central letter of the word for fool is removed

parts.note: a moron is a fool

explanation.surface: A callous idiot makes an obscene sign.
explanation.walkthrough: To moon is to bare one's backside at someone as an insult.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooning is exposing the buttocks as an insult or prank.

clue.text: Scared female put back on the correct path

parts.words: put back on the correct path
parts.note: to righten is an old verb meaning to set right or restore

explanation.surface: A frightened woman is guided back onto the right route.
explanation.definitionFit: Afraid and fearful describe someone startled into alarm.

clue.text: Great person seen as evil over time

indicators.note: over means covering, so the word for evil wraps around the letter for time

parts.note: immoral means wicked or evil

explanation.surface: A celebrated figure is regarded as wicked over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Legends and greats are remembered forever, and are hence called the undying.

clue.text: Cheat acted, having got led astray

parts.note: did means acted, as in did something

indicators.note: astray means wandering off course, so the letters of led are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swindler performed after being misled.
explanation.definitionFit: To diddle is British slang for to swindle someone.
